findings.title: OTP Verification Bypass on Invalid Code
findings.description: The server accepted an obviously invalid OTP code ('000000') or returned 200 OK without verification.
findings.expected: Server must respond with HTTP 401 Unauthorized or 400 Bad Request.
findings.impact: Complete authentication bypass enabling account takeover without valid second factor.
findings.remediation: Enforce strict cryptographic comparison of OTP secrets and reject unverified codes.

findings.title: OTP Replay / Reuse Vulnerability
findings.description: The server permitted reuse of an already submitted One-Time Password.
findings.expected: OTPs must be single-use and immediately consumed/invalidated upon first verification.
findings.actual: Server accepted identical OTP on subsequent verification request.
findings.impact: Attackers intercepting an OTP can reuse it to authenticate.
findings.remediation: Mark OTP tokens as consumed in the database immediately upon successful verification.

findings.title: Missing OTP Attempt Rate Limiting
findings.description: Endpoint permitted 5 consecutive invalid OTP attempts without rate-limiting (HTTP 429) or lockout.
findings.expected: After 3-5 incorrect attempts, server should return HTTP 429 or lock the verification session.
findings.impact: Increases susceptibility to automated 4-6 digit OTP brute-force attacks.
findings.remediation: Enforce strict per-account and per-IP attempt limits (max 3-5 failed tries per OTP).

findings.title: Unbound OTP Verification State
findings.description: Server accepted OTP verification without user account or session binding.
findings.expected: Server must require authenticated session or explicit user binding.
findings.impact: Cross-user OTP acceptance enabling lateral privilege escalation.
findings.remediation: Bind OTP secrets strictly to the server-side session of the authenticating user.

findings.title: Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint
findings.description: Authentication endpoint '/login' processed repeated invalid logins without returning HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests), rate-limit headers, or progressive backoff.
findings.expected: Server should return HTTP 429 or enforce temporary lockout after 5 failed login attempts.
findings.actual: Endpoint returned standard rejection statuses without rate limiting: [401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401]
findings.impact: Enables automated offline/online credential testing and password guessing attacks.
findings.remediation: Implement IP and username based rate limiting (e.g., token bucket or leaky bucket algorithm) returning HTTP 429.

findings.title: Authentication Account Enumeration Weakness
findings.description: The authentication endpoint returns distinguishable error messages or status codes for valid usernames versus invalid usernames, allowing adversaries to enumerate valid accounts.
findings.expected: Server must return uniform error messages (e.g., 'Invalid credentials') and identical HTTP status codes.
findings.actual: Existing user status: 401, Nonexistent user status: 404
findings.impact: Allows attackers to harvest valid corporate usernames for targeted spear-phishing or credential attacks.
findings.remediation: Normalize all authentication failure messages and response times to be indistinguishable.

findings.title: Missing Server-Side CAPTCHA Enforcement
findings.description: Authentication endpoint '/login' accepted an authentication request without requiring a CAPTCHA response token.
findings.expected: Server must validate that a valid CAPTCHA token accompanies the request and reject submissions missing the token with HTTP 400 or 422.
findings.actual: Server processed request without CAPTCHA token and returned HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Enables automated bot attacks, credential stuffing, and scripted login workflows.
findings.remediation: Enforce mandatory server-side verification of CAPTCHA tokens with the provider before processing credentials.

findings.title: Forged CAPTCHA Token Accepted
findings.description: Server accepted a fabricated CAPTCHA token without validating its signature with the CAPTCHA verification API.
findings.expected: Server must query verification provider and reject unauthorized/forged tokens.
findings.actual: Server accepted forged token and returned HTTP 200.
findings.impact: Completely negates anti-bot protections by permitting static dummy tokens.
findings.remediation: Validate every token server-side via the provider secret key and verify success: true.

findings.title: CAPTCHA Token Replay / Reuse Vulnerability
findings.description: The server permitted reuse of an already submitted CAPTCHA token across multiple requests.
findings.expected: CAPTCHA tokens must be strictly single-use and rejected on subsequent attempts.
findings.actual: Server accepted previously submitted CAPTCHA token on re-use attempt.
findings.impact: Attackers can solve a single CAPTCHA and replay the token to automate multiple requests.
findings.remediation: Ensure CAPTCHA tokens are consumed or enforce provider timestamp and hostname validation.
